newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Trade in Banespa remains suspended.
newsitem.headline: Trade in Banespa remains suspended.

text.p: Trade in shares of Sao Paulo state bank Banespa remains suspended and bourse officials are discussing this morning when it will resume, the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa) said.

Banespa shares have been suspended since Tuesday after a newspaper reported the bank had a 786.3 million real net profit in the first nine months, which led the bourse and Brazil's Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM) to request a clarification.

The bourse officials are also digesting an agreement sealed yesterday between Sao Paulo state and the federal government allowing the transfer of Banespa to federal hands under a major debt rescheduling plan.

Sao Paulo state will sell a 51 percent stake in Banespa to the federal government for a price to be determined after one year. While under federal control, the bank will be run by an independent manager which will be hired in a bidding process.
The deal, however, still needs approval from state and federal lawmakers.

Brazil's largest state bank, Banespa has been under Central Bank management since December 1994 due to financial troubles caused by Sao Paulo state's huge debt with it. -- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom, 55-11-2485412
